description: Modelling, predicting, and choosing: machine learning, neural networks, language models, and the questions they raise.

concepts.title: Intelligence
concepts.summary: The ability to model a situation, predict what comes next, and choose what to do. Machines have imitated slivers of it for decades, and lately the slivers have grown broad enough to be useful and strange.

concepts.title: Machine Learning
concepts.summary: Instead of writing rules, show a system many examples and let it adjust itself to fit them. The result can spot patterns no one described, and it can also inherit every flaw in the examples.

concepts.title: Pattern Recognition
concepts.summary: Finding regularity in noise: a face in pixels, a word in sound, a tumor in a scan. It's what brains do effortlessly and what machines had to learn slowly.

concepts.title: Neural Networks
concepts.summary: Layers of simple units, each passing a weighted signal to the next. Loosely inspired by neurons, they learn by nudging millions of weights until the output improves.

concepts.title: Language Models
concepts.summary: Systems trained on huge amounts of text to predict what comes next in a sentence. From that one task they pick up grammar, facts, and style, along with a habit of sounding sure when they aren't.

concepts.title: Attention
concepts.summary: In machines, a way for a model to weigh which parts of its input matter for each step. In people, the older version: what you attend to is what your world becomes.

concepts.title: Reasoning
concepts.summary: Getting from what you know to something you didn't, in steps you could defend. People do it slowly and imperfectly; machines can do it fast, but doing it reliably in open situations is still hard.

concepts.title: Turing Test
concepts.summary: Turing's proposal: if you can't tell a machine from a person by conversation alone, stop arguing about whether it thinks. It became a landmark, and a reminder that fooling someone and understanding are different things.

concepts.title: Alignment
concepts.summary: Making sure a capable system does what its makers and users actually want, not just what they literally said. It's partly engineering and partly the old human problem of saying what we mean.

concepts.title: Automation
concepts.summary: Handing a repeatable task to a machine so nobody has to do it. It frees time and removes work, and it also changes who has the skill, who gets paid, and what people think is worth learning.
